title: Armenian Manuscript (Armenien 128)
shelf_note: An Armenian manuscript catalogued as Armenian. The page is hagiography in a handwritten Armenian hand. No tradition or collection is given to test it against.
structure_note: Only 282 of 582 records carry a printed number, so the 14 backsteps and 17 repeats most likely come from pencil foliation that was misread or written irregularly, not from a broken sequence. The counts disagree with each other: structure pages_translated is 0, but the book field says 554 (E2). The OCR <vocab> says '14th century manuscript', which nothing on this paper leaf supports.

pages.layout: two ruled columns; a small two-line marginal note left of column 1 at about line 13; first line of column 2 struck through; several faded or erased lines below column 2; pencil number 271 at the foot

ocr_errors.image: the first line of column 2 is struck through in ink
ocr_errors.problem: a cancelled line is transcribed as running text with no deletion mark, so the translation reads it as part of the narrative ('He went forth before glory')

ocr_errors.image: below the last line of column 2 there are several faded or erased lines and a short final line
ocr_errors.problem: the faded lines are left out with no lacuna or illegibility marker

ocr_errors.ocr: Բաղումէ ... Բաղով ... ըստ Բաղայ ... Բաղայեալ ... Բաղում ... Բաղեաց ... Բաղյ ... Բաղա
ocr_errors.image: at this resolution the hand cannot be checked word by word
ocr_errors.problem: a stem 'Բաղ-' recurs about ten times in forms that do not hang together grammatically. That is a typical sign of a misread repeated across the page. Column 2 also seems to have about 22 lines on the image against 20 in the OCR. I cannot confirm either point.

other.note: a raw <column-break/> tag sits in the middle of the English reader text
the English contains '<margin>Note</margin>', a single marginal word rendered as 'Note' and placed inside the sentence ('they struck <margin>Note</margin> his two')
the OCR <vocab> asserts '14th century manuscript', a date that is not on the leaf

missing.english:
the holy
Cross was revealed, which is at <unclear>Varag</unclear>
missing.why: the Holy Cross of Varag is an Armenian relic tradition, and a general reader will not know what Varag is or why its Cross matters
nothing tells the reader that this is a marginal annotation in the manuscript, or what it marks

book_verdict: The leaf matches its record: two columns of Armenian hagiography with pencil foliation 271. I could not check the bolorgir word by word at this resolution, and the OCR looks shaky (a repeated 'Բաղ-' stem, a struck-through line kept as text, faded lines dropped). The English hedges heavily with <unclear>, but it shows a raw <column-break/> and carries no notes.
